title: BLACKWOOD ARTS & CRAFTS SIDEBOARD...
reason: Well figured Arts and Crafts blackwood furniture of a useful size with local appeal; condition and form need a viewing. Value band is my estimate only.
findings: Two photos of a three-bay Arts and Crafts side cabinet or dresser in what looks like figured Tasmanian blackwood (consistent with the title): two panelled cupboard pedestals either side of a central pair of long drawers with twin flat brass bar pulls each, a recessed shelf above the drawers, and a stepped upstand with two tall panelled wings and a central raised bevelled mirror plate. Square tapering legs on stepped plinth feet, shaped pointed-arch bracket aprons between the legs, simple mouldings and panel-and-frame construction typical of Federation to 1910s Australian work. Drawer and door fronts show a lively fiddleback or curl figure. No maker's label, stamp or retailer's mark is visible in the two photos (back, drawer interiors and undersides not shown). No door pulls or knobs are visible on the two cupboard doors (missing, or catches). The close up shows a chipped vertical strip with exposed rough timber at the junction of the drawer section and the right-hand pedestal, and the foot blocks look like later additions or repairs on darker leg ends.
condition: Wear, light scratching and fading to both pedestal tops and the upstand; chipped or broken vertical strip at the right drawer pedestal junction; foot blocks look replaced or added and are stained dark; no door furniture visible; mirror plate bevelled and clean. Looks sound overall but back, drawer runners and top fixings are not shown.
rescore_note: Well figured blackwood Arts and Crafts side cabinet with local appeal, but plain construction, missing door pulls, replaced foot blocks and a chipped strip; timber and maker unverified and large brown furniture sells soft.
